Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. 197	## Exclude content from a prefetch
198	
199	Optimizing a prefetch also means excluding content from it. Some subtrees are expensive enough to produce that you would rather not pay for them on every prefetch of the route.
200	
201	Awaiting [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) above the work leaves it out of every prefetch, so it is produced on the navigation. The nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) fallback is what the user sees while it streams in. Take the dashboard again, where a ranking keyed on the session is too expensive to produce for every link into the route:
202	
203	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx" highlight={6}
204	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
205	import { navigation } from 'next/cache'
206	
207	async function Recommendations() {
208	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
209	  await navigation()
210	  const items = await rank(session)
211	  return <List items={items} />
212	}
213	
214	async function rank(session?: string) {
215	  'use cache: private'
216	  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
217	}
218	```
219	
220	The session is read above `navigation()`, so it resolves in the shell like any other session data. Only the ranking is left out, and it keeps its cache lifetime.
221	
222	Without it, keeping a subtree out of a prefetch means leaving it uncached, which gives up that lifetime on the navigation too. Awaiting `navigation()` inside a cached scope is not allowed, so put the caching directive on a function called below it, as `rank` does here.
223	
224	For a subtree that would otherwise sit in the App Shell, but that a `<Link prefetch={true}>` should still resolve before the click, use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) instead.
225	
226	Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), `navigation()` does not make the subtree request-dependent. This lets reusable content keep its cache lifetime while waiting for navigation. See [How `navigation()` differs from `connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation#how-navigation-differs-from-connection) for the full comparison.
227	
228	## Test prefetched and deferred content
229	
230	The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) explains how to install and configure `@next/playwright`. For a client navigation, use `instant()` to inspect the destination's prefetched UI.
231	
232	When [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests), run this test before enabling the feature and rerun the same assertions afterward. This preserves the UI selected from the legacy full prefetch while its implementation moves to the App Shell or a per-link prefetch.
233	
234	Inside the callback, click the link, wait for the destination URL, and assert which content is available. After the callback releases the navigation, assert that deferred content eventually renders:
235	
236	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={8-15,17}
237	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
238	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
239	
240	test('prefetches the product summary but not reviews', async ({ page }) => {
241	  await page.goto('/products')
242	
243	  await instant(page, async () => {
244	    await page.click('a[href="/products/baseball-cap"]')
245	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
246	
247	    await expect(
248	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
249	    ).toBeVisible()
250	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
251	    await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toHaveCount(0)
252	  })
253	
254	  await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toBeVisible()
255	})
256	```
257	
258	While the `instant()` callback is running, dynamic content is paused. In this example, the product summary is part of the prefetched UI, while reviews wait for navigation. The final assertion confirms that the reviews render after the pause is released.
259	
260	## Trade-offs
261	
262	Use `prefetch={true}` on routes where:
263	
264	- Part of the component tree depends on URL data: the full URL, `searchParams`, or `params` not resolved by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)
265	- That part of the tree has a known cache lifetime (it can be expressed with `"use cache"` or `"use cache: private"`)
266	- The traffic justifies the per-link server invocation
267	
268	Prefetching cached data does not change its freshness behavior. If a mutation can update the data, [tag and invalidate the cached result](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating).
269	
270	Skip it when the prefetch can't produce a better UI than the App Shell. Each visible `<Link prefetch={true}>` can wake a server, and that cost only pays off if more of the page is ready before the click:
271	
272	- The route has little or no URL-data dependency. The App Shell already makes the navigation instant.
273	- The dependent content has to be fresh on every request. The prerender stops at the same `<Suspense>` fallback, so the user sees the same UI either way.
274	- The route is rarely navigated to. You pay per visible link, regardless of click-through.
275	
276	A per-link prefetch is best-effort. It only helps the navigations where it completes before the click. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, it may not be ready when the user navigates, and the navigation falls back to the App Shell.

281	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
282	| Scope   | One per route                               | One per visible `<Link prefetch={true}>` |
283	| Content | Route's rendered output minus per-link data | Same, plus per-link URL data resolved    |
284	| Cost    | Bounded by route count                      | Bounded by visible-link count            |
285	| Role    | Default prefetch                            | More rendered before click               |
286	
287	[Excluding content](#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) is one more control on top of these. The trade is generating content for a prefetch that may never be used, against momentarily showing a `<Suspense>` fallback while that content streams in.

12	---
13	
14	`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	  partialPrefetching: true,
24	}
25	
26	export default nextConfig
27	```
28	
29	```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher
30	module.exports = {
31	  cacheComponents: true,
32	  partialPrefetching: true,
33	}
34	```
35	
36	`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
37	
38	## Reference
39	
40	| Value   | Description                                 |
41	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
42	| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
43	| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |
44	
45	## How prefetches resolve
46	
47	Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
48	
49	With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
50	
51	The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
52	
53	> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
54	
55	A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
56	
57	> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
58	
59	## Per-segment overrides
60	
61	A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                     |
66	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
</content>
